entry_conditions: Use the demonstrated world-frame Panda state and absolute joint-target controller with both block poses/goals visible. This policy covers the FULL expanded delivery slices, including pre-grasp open descent. Measured starts have the selected source block at z=0.020 m, TCP z=0.0877-0.1779 m and fingers near 0.040 m each. These are observed support, not hard admission thresholds. It can also enter during closing, initial lift or elevated transport. The supplied forward interface has no external payload token: soft TCP/object proximity roles and each object's goal status infer the intended payload/pending identity from causal state. Do not assume it can resolve an arbitrary requested identity inconsistent with those cues. Provide two actual causal observations with qpos/qvel (0:18), TCP pose (18:25), red/blue poses (25:39) and goals (41:47), positions in world metres and quaternions wxyz. At empty descent the observed relative transform exists geometrically but is explicitly invalid for carried-payload decoding. Validity requires closed/near/stable two-state geometry plus lift-compatible or moving-together evidence, not merely proximity or a closed command.
exit_conditions: Geometric completion and manipulation readiness are different. Formal task success is exactly red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal under the supplied full rotated XY containment and z tolerance; it can hold near object z=0.0455 m while still grasped, and does not require release, TCP clearance, low velocity or a sustained hold. For continued manipulation, the useful demonstrated exit is the selected object settled near z=0.036 m, fingers opening toward 0.040 m each, and object no longer following TCP retreat. After red the expanded slice includes open retreat and approach toward blue with TCP z about 0.267 m. After final blue it includes empty retreat toward z about 0.3165 m and hold. These measured exit heights guide a useful handoff, not extra task-success predicates or exact commanded waypoints.
overlap_role: The model learns open descent, closure and early lift in the initial acquisition/delivery overlaps, using unconditional path/action supervision even when attachment is invalid. Co-motion in these overlaps identifies the actual TCP-to-object offset before transport. The shared final lowering/opening/settling/retreat/next-approach phases permit either continued delivery or transfer to acquisition while the transform is transitioning from attached to invalid. The complete expanded slices are retained without phase filtering. Examples of supplied overlap support are demo10300 [75,182), [265,415), [445,562), and demo10307 [72,178), [259,408), [439,552); analogous measured overlaps exist in all twelve training demonstrations. These are evidence about training support, not an execution timetable.
successor_readiness: For next acquisition, retain both object identities/goals, the actual qpos/qvel, actual finger positions, TCP pose and two-state TCP/object motion. Blue is pending after red in these demonstrations, but this implementation infers pending roles from current object goal cues rather than a color clock. If transferred before release, the successor must receive evidence that red is still attached and be able to finish lowering/opening. If transferred after release, preserve the open-hand state and blue-source geometry; do not impose a closed payload-conditioned action or reset coordinate frames. At late red-to-blue transfer the demonstrated command remains +1 during empty approach. After final blue, both object goal predicates may already end the task regardless of whether the optional empty retreat has finished.
failure_signatures: Treat TCP-at-marker with a block offset/outside containment, wrong-object motion, abrupt arm-target branch changes, changing estimated C during nominal rigid carry, or an object following retreat after expected release as uncertainty. Closed fingers near a stationary table object do not establish a grasp; stable co-motion after lift is stronger evidence but still not a contact measurement. The model uses internal validity cues but exports no calibrated uncertainty channel or verified recovery action. Unsupported failures should trigger observation-based reassessment rather than an assumption of automatic IK or collision correction.
continuation_guidance: Continue this learned policy when observations show an unfinished supported descent/close/lift/carry/lower/release transition, including entry partway through an overlap. The model conditions on both causal observations and current world state, not elapsed source indices. Inspect fingers and whether the object moves with TCP before treating it as attached or released. An acquisition successor may take over within the trained late-placement overlap if it can complete the observed transition; otherwise delivery can continue through empty retreat and open approach toward the pending block. If both formal containment predicates hold, the task is complete without requiring further release/retreat. The runtime remains H=16 with eight executed actions per invocation; this implementation does not implement the original proposed one-to-two-action placement resampling.
limitations: Observed support is local to the demonstrated top-down Panda manifold and small grasp-offset variation. Only two causal state observations, no command history, explicit identity token, force sensor, image, FK or IK are available. The Cartesian path is a learned latent inside mandatory joint-action DDPM, not an independently sampled Cartesian DDPM. Relative transforms and role weights may be wrong or ambiguous outside support. Inference uses no future observations; future states supply only masked training targets. Shared complete-demonstration normalization is preserved. Learned inverse dynamics and bounded normalized proposals do not guarantee feasibility, smoothness, collision safety, containment, rotational generalization or recovery. Interface validation alone is not behavioral success evidence.
